correctness.rationale: The even and odd defect-site resolvent eigenvalues are strictly decreasing, positive and tend to zero. Only the even one diverges at the edge; the odd one has finite positive limit g_r(E_*). Positivity of the off-diagonal resolvent (for example by the lattice walk series) orders the two branches and excludes a double root. At V_c the inverse Fourier transform of (1−exp(−ik·r))/q(k) has defect values g_r(E_*) and −g_r(E_*), so solves the threshold equation and is odd under u↦r−u. Its transform is L¹ but not L², by a lower bound on an angular sector on which |k·r| is comparable to |k|. An L² threshold solution cannot have a nonzero constant or dipole source at the edge, so no threshold eigenvector is missed. For the subtracted integral the Taylor remainders are O(δ) after integration. In the scaled low-frequency disk the factor 1/2 from 1−cos, the angular integral π(m²/t_x+n²/t_y), the radial factor (1/2)log(1/δ), the Jacobian and the normalized measure yield (m²/t_x+n²/t_y)/(16π√(t_xt_y)). Inversion against (V−V_c)/V_c² gives the claimed limit. The resistance factor is two, from the squared dipole numerator. Integrating one Fourier variable and substituting the half-angle in the other gives the two arctangents, including 9 and 6 for (3,1).
residual_risks: The numerical comparisons are finite corroboration, not interval certificates or finite-box error bounds. The asymptotic holds at fixed positive hoppings and fixed nonzero displacement, not uniformly in those parameters.

value.rationale: For a natural two-site lattice model the result separates the one-mode and two-mode regimes and gives the rate of detachment, not just the threshold location. The coefficient distinguishes orientations and displacement at fixed anisotropy and explains the logarithmic suppression due to the critical odd resonance. These are quantitative predictions for a localized mode absent from a static resistance computation.
residual_risks: No implication for unequal defects, nonuniform hoppings or an anisotropy/displacement scaling limit is established.
